description:
Approved by the user 2026-11-17 ("approved; two allocations is dopey"), proposed by the GC session from fz-9x7.24.

Measured (fz-9x7.24, leak A/B, 7 interleaved runs, counters only): destroying one binary in survive costs ~304 instructions / ~300 cycles; 200k destructions are 14% of the program's cycles. Each makes two system-malloc frees: the 1025-byte buffer and the 48-byte SharedBin box.

Change: lay a SharedBin out as one block, header then bytes then room (as BEAM's Binary). Halves allocations and frees per binary and removes the bytes_ptr pointer chase.

Rule (fixed before measuring): gate green; survive instructions fall >= 5% (prediction 7%); nothing rises beyond noise; in-use bytes (fz-9x7.16) do not rise beyond 48 B x live binaries.

Room path (read on develop, runtime/src/heap/imp.rs:963-1001 alloc_concatenation): a SharedBin buffer is never reallocated or swapped; nothing assigns bytes_ptr after creation. In-place append only when right.len() <= spare() of the fixed capacity; otherwise a NEW SharedBin with room total*2 (the GrownBuffer site). So the header address never changes. Grow means a new block, never a realloc; fz-sc8.111's page keeps that.

Watch: grown-buffer stubs keep their identity; static compiler-baked SharedBins stay separate with their no-op destructor. fz-9x7.8's trigger reads capacity() from the header (same quantity, read site moves with it); overlap with .8 only at imp.rs binary allocation sites, second to land rebases.
Files: runtime/src/bits.rs, runtime/src/heap/imp.rs, off_heap.rs.
title: A shared binary is one allocation: its header followed by its bytes
